_about: Plain-English reason wording for a new applicant (Decision 30). Single source of truth for the API (serving/app.py), the dashboard (dashboard/scoring.py) and the public site (website/public/assets/reasons.js). Each input has wording for when the applicant's value is lower or higher than the typical applicant's. Wording describes what the model links to risk; it never claims cause and never mentions the review cutoff.

monthly_income_gbp.label: your monthly income
monthly_income_gbp.lower: Your monthly income of {value} is lower than is typical for applicants ({typical}).
monthly_income_gbp.higher: Your monthly income of {value} is higher than is typical for applicants ({typical}).

existing_monthly_obligations_gbp.label: your existing monthly repayments
existing_monthly_obligations_gbp.lower: You pay {value} a month towards other commitments, less than is typical ({typical}).
existing_monthly_obligations_gbp.higher: You already pay {value} a month towards other commitments, more than is typical ({typical}).

savings_balance_gbp.label: your savings
savings_balance_gbp.lower: Your savings of {value} are lower than is typical ({typical}), leaving less to fall back on if money gets tight.
savings_balance_gbp.higher: Your savings of {value} are higher than is typical ({typical}).

credit_score.label: your credit score
credit_score.lower: Your credit score of {value} is lower than is typical for applicants ({typical}).
credit_score.higher: Your credit score of {value} is higher than is typical for applicants ({typical}).

months_credit_history.label: the length of your credit history
months_credit_history.lower: Your credit history covers {value}, shorter than is typical ({typical}).
months_credit_history.higher: Your credit history covers {value}, longer than is typical ({typical}).

num_credit_accounts.label: your number of credit accounts
num_credit_accounts.lower: You have {value}, fewer than is typical ({typical}).
num_credit_accounts.higher: You have {value}, more than is typical ({typical}).

num_defaults_24m.label: your recent repayment record
num_defaults_24m.lower: Your credit file shows {value} in the last two years, fewer than is typical ({typical}).
num_defaults_24m.higher: Your credit file shows {value} in the last two years.

thin_file_flag.label: the depth of your credit file
thin_file_flag.lower: Your credit file has a full borrowing history.
thin_file_flag.higher: Your credit file has limited borrowing history, so there is less evidence of how you manage repayments.

order_value_gbp.label: the size of this order
order_value_gbp.lower: This order of {value} is smaller than a typical order ({typical}).
order_value_gbp.higher: This order of {value} is larger than a typical order ({typical}).

n_instalments.label: the repayment plan
n_instalments.lower: You chose to repay over {value}, fewer than is typical ({typical}).
n_instalments.higher: You chose to spread repayments over {value}, more than is typical ({typical}).

merchant_category.label: the type of purchase
merchant_category.lower: This purchase is in the {value} category.
merchant_category.higher: This purchase is in the {value} category, which the model links to more missed repayments than {typical} purchases.

refer.title: Why this application was referred for review
refer.intro: The application has been passed to a person to review; it has not been declined. The details that counted most against it were:
refer.link: The model links each of these to a higher chance of falling behind on repayments.
refer.none: No single detail stood out; it was the combination of details that the model linked to a higher chance of falling behind on repayments.

pass.title: Why this application was not referred
pass.intro: The model did not flag this application for review. The details that counted most in its favour were:
pass.none: No single detail stood out; the details taken together were not flagged.
pass.against_intro: Details the model linked to higher risk, though not enough to flag it:

refer: Check these details are correct. If any are wrong, ask for them to be corrected before the review.
A referral is not a decline: a reviewer looks at the whole application.
This explains how the model scored these details on synthetic data. It is not financial advice.
pass: This explains how the model scored these details on synthetic data. It is not financial advice.
